note: EXPERIMENTAL v2. Ordered-probit refit of HumanFB: 5-level categorical ratings modelled as thresholds (tau) on a latent difference axis; per-pair latent mean mu and observer-spread sigma. mu = mu_scale*de (Spearman 0.957); sigma = a*de + b*chroma + c (latent units, LOO-R2 0.49, log-sigma ridge lambda=2). Replaces v1, whose disagreement target (std of category codes) was ANTI-correlated (rho=-0.51) with the latent observer spread — a ceiling-pile-up artifact. Relative disagreement sigma/mu falls with de (rho=-0.77) and chroma (-0.36): small / low-chroma differences remain the unreliable regime. Chroma sign caveat: absolute sigma RISES with chroma; hong_2025 between-observer JND CV agrees in sign (+0.23), but threshold vs suprathreshold domains differ - do not over-read the chroma axis. p_noticeable = P(latent > tau[1]) ~ chance a random observer rates the pair at least 'moderately different'.
